Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
QXE...@prodigy.com (Shawn Mccollum) writes:

>Someone told me that you can use a sudden reversal to get rid of a master
>card that has been on the table for rounds. Is this True? If so I think
>it Sucks.
>Also is there a list of rulings some where on the net?

An ancient Design Team Ruling said that Sudden Reversal could remove a
card in play. This was reversed back in 11/9/95. Sudden Reversal can
only counter a Matser Card *as the master card is played*.

Messages.Author: Joseph Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3ih4lk$14...@usenetw1.news.prodigy.com>,

Shawn Mccollum <QXE...@prodigy.com> wrote:
>Someone told me that you can use a sudden reversal to get rid of a master
>card that has been on the table for rounds. Is this True? If so I think
>it Sucks.

No, it's not. It was for a while, but the Rules Team came back
with a statement that it has to be used like a counterspell.

>Also is there a list of rulings some where on the net?
